lines: The AI wrote workspace B on its request. The server crossed it out.
To save a memory, an AI sends two ids: the message it came from, and its chat. Nothing ties them. One wrong guess, or one buggy client, and a real message lands in the wrong chat.
Both ids come from the same writer. Only the server's records know which chat that message is in.

So the server stops asking. The model sends the message id. The server looks it up in its own records and stamps the chat from there. Same rule for the workspace: it comes from who's signed in. Put B in the request, and the write still lands in A.
One real memory tool asks for six fields, all required. Chat id isn't one of them. Its description says why: derived on the server.
It won't prove the AI picked the right message. It stops one thing: that message in the wrong chat. Let the model choose. Make the server decide.
